literature.headline_zh: 诺如病毒研究进展:跨物种传播、流行病学特征及监测技术。
literature.lead_zh: 近期研究涵盖了诺如病毒的跨物种传播机制、临床流行病学特征、环境暴露途径以及先进的监测与培养技术。
key_findings_zh: 研究发现人类诺如病毒在猪和狗的肠道组织中具有较高的结合与内化能力,且能在猪肠道中复制,提示人与动物间存在跨物种传播风险 [10.1080/22221751.2026.2713851]。
在英格兰的观察显示,诺如病毒的病死风险主要与年龄和护理环境相关,而非病毒基因型 [10.3201/eid3208.260091]。
废水监测被证实是监测诺如病毒有效的早期预警工具,其废水浓度与住院率呈显著正相关,且领先住院率约两周 [10.14745/ccdr.v52i78a04]。
通过在人肠类中同时使用 JAK 抑制剂和趋化因子拮抗剂,可以显著增强 GII.17 诺如病毒的复制并实现连续传代 [10.1111/gtc.70139]。
研究发现沿海冲浪区可能通过气溶胶化成为废水相关微生物的暴露途径,PMMoV 可作为此类环境中气溶胶病毒的可靠指标 [10.1016/j.envpol.2026.128860]。
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险点包括人畜共患传播的可能性、老化的水利基础设施导致的食源性暴发风险,以及通过气溶胶进行空气传播的潜在风险。
literature.caveats_zh: 部分研究基于离体模型或实验室环境,可能无法完全模拟体内或复杂的现实环境条件。
literature.headline_en: Advances in Norovirus Research: Cross-species Transmission, Epidemiology, and Monitoring Technologies.
literature.lead_en: Recent studies cover human norovirus cross-species transmission, clinical epidemiological characteristics, environmental exposure pathways, and advanced monitoring and cultivation techniques.
key_findings_en: Human norovirus shows high binding and internalization efficiency in porcine and canine intestinal tissues and replicates in pig tissue, suggesting potential for cross-species transmission [10.1080/22221751.2026.2713851].
In England, case-fatality risk for norovirus was associated with age and care setting rather than viral genotype [10.3201/eid3208.260091].

Wastewater surveillance is a valid tool for population-level monitoring, with wastewater concentrations significantly correlating with hospitalizations and leading them by two weeks [10.14745/ccdr.v52i78a04].
Simultaneous inhibition of JAK and chemokine signaling pathways in human intestinal enteroids significantly enhances GII.17 norovirus replication and enables serial passaging [10.1111/gtc.70139].

Coastal surf zones may serve as interfaces for the aerosolization of wastewater-associated microorganisms, with PMMoV acting as a reliable indicator for aerosolized viruses [10.1016/j.envpol.2026.128860].
literature.trend_or_risk_en: Risks include potential zoonotic transmission, foodborne outbreaks due to aging water infrastructure, and inhalation exposure via aerosolized wastewater in coastal areas.
literature.caveats_en: Some findings are based on ex vivo models or laboratory settings, which may not fully recapitulate in vivo or complex real-world environmental conditions.
literature.brief_en: Recent research highlights the potential for human-to-animal norovirus transmission, the effectiveness of wastewater surveillance for early warning, and new methods to enhance in vitro virus cultivation.

news.headline_zh: 诺如病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期诺如病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 研究小组成功生产了人类 诺如病毒 GII.3 毒株的病毒样颗粒 (VLP),并使用冷冻电子显微镜确定了其结构,揭示了病毒衣壳的两种不同的构象状态(静止和上升)。 [news-46532d551580c2c4]
Moderna 的研究性 mRNA 诺如病毒 疫苗 候选药物 (mRNA-1403) 的 3 期试验未达到早期成功的统计标准,但试验将继续进行。 [news-3237523b682ca79f]

Cocrystal Pharma secured a $5 million investment from OPKO Health, Inc. (Nasdaq: OPK), a longtime investor, as the company advances its norovirus program toward Phase 1b clinical trial data expected by late 2026. [news-fb05ddfbf7f6b883]
Moderna 的 mRNA-1403 诺如病毒 疫苗 未能达到第 3 期中期分析中早期成功的预先指定的统计阈值,将试验延长至第四个入组季节;确认是临时失误,而非疗效失败。 [news-3500f55aecdf20d5]
Moderna 宣布其 mRNA 诺如病毒 疫苗 的 3 期试验未达到早期成功标准。这项研究仍在继续,一组新的志愿者正在招募进行冬季测试。 [news-1fad23fd28d111c8]
news.trend_or_risk_zh: 风险判断仅依据入选来源已经确认的信息，不把媒体推测升级为官方结论。
news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Norovirus news developments.
key_findings_en: A research team successfully produced virus-like particles (VLPs) of the human norovirus GII.3 strain and determined their structures using cryo-electron microscopy, revealing two distinct conformational states (resting and rising) of the virus capsid. [news-46532d551580c2c4]
Moderna's phase 3 trial for its investigational mRNA norovirus vaccine candidate (mRNA-1403) did not meet statistical criteria for early success, but the trial will continue. [news-3237523b682ca79f]

Cocrystal Pharma secured a $5 million investment from OPKO Health, Inc. papers.title: Comparative Clinical and Molecular Epidemiology of Norovirus in Hospitalized Gastroenteritis Cases, Western India (2013-2023).
papers.abstract: Following widespread vaccination against Rotavirus A (RVA), Norovirus (NoV) has emerged as a leading cause of acute gastroenteritis (AGE). However, data on the clinical characteristics and molecular epidemiology of NoV in India remain limited. A total of 1637 fecal samples from hospitalized sporadic AGE cases collected between April 2013 and May 2023 from two cities each in Maharashtra and Gujarat, India, were screened for NoV. Positive samples were characterized by molecular genotyping. NoV was detected in 149 (9.1%) cases, with 123 (82.5%) infections occurring in children under 2 years of age. Most patients 103 (69.1%) had severe or very severe illness, and 22.8% had mixed viral infections, predominantly with RVA. Genotyping identified 11 VP1 genotypes, 9 RdRp P-types, and approximately 30 genotype combinations, demonstrating substantial genetic diversity. GII.4 (n = 66) and GII.P16 (n = 67) were the predominant variants and were associated with more severe disease than less common genotypes. The validated qRT-PCR assays demonstrated > 97% sensitivity and specificity for regional strains, enabling rapid and accurate diagnosis. The extensive genetic diversity of NoV circulating in Indian children highlights the need for enhanced molecular surveillance, improved diagnostics, and consideration of locally prevalent genotypes in future vaccine development.

analysis.study_design_and_population: A total of 1637 fecal samples from hospitalized sporadic AGE cases collected between April 2013 and May 2023 from two cities each in Maharashtra and Gujarat, India, were screened for NoV. Positive samples were characterized by molecular genotyping.
analysis.methods: The validated qRT-PCR assays demonstrated > 97% sensitivity and specificity for regional strains, enabling rapid and accurate diagnosis.
analysis.main_results: NoV was detected in 149 (9.1%) cases, with 123 (82.5%) infections occurring in children under 2 years of age. GII.4 (n = 66) and GII.P16 (n = 67) were the predominant variants and were associated with more severe disease than less common genotypes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The extensive genetic diversity of NoV circulating in Indian children highlights the need for enhanced molecular surveillance, improved diagnostics, and consideration of locally prevalent genotypes in future vaccine development.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings demonstrate the importance of understanding NoV genetic diversity for improving diagnostics and vaccine development in the context of India's changing epidemiology of acute gastroenteritis.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design and reliance on fecal samples from hospitalized cases, which may not represent the full spectrum of NoV infections. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the clinical and molecular epidemiology of Norovirus (NoV) in hospitalized gastroenteritis cases in Western India from 2013 to 2023. It highlights the increasing role of NoV as a cause of acute gastroenteritis following Rotavirus A (RVA) vaccination. The research found that NoV was detected in 9.1% of cases, predominantly in children under 2 years of age, with GII.4 and GII.P16 variants associated with more severe disease. The study emphasizes the genetic diversity of NoV in the region and calls for enhanced molecular surveillance and improved diagnostics. The findings suggest the need for considering locally prevalent genotypes in vaccine development. However, the study's retrospective design and focus on hospitalized cases limit its generalizability, and the evidence is moderate in strength.

papers.title: Norovirus inter-species transmission in an ex vivo model is dependent on virus internalization capacity.
papers.abstract: Human noroviruses (HuNoV) are the most common cause of viral gastroenteritis worldwide, causing sporadic cases and outbreaks. Noroviruses that infect wild and domestic animals, including pigs and dogs, are genetically related to human noroviruses, increasing the potential for cross-species transmission. To investigate the potential of noroviruses to cross the species barrier, we used porcine, canine, and avian precision-cut intestinal slices. We show that human norovirus virus-like particles (VLPs) bind to pig and dog intestinal tissue and are taken up with a similar efficiency as the porcine and canine noroviruses, respectively. In contrast, no binding or internalization of human, porcine, or canine noroviruses was detected in chicken tissue. We further showed that human norovirus replicates in pig intestinal tissue. In contrast, while animal noroviruses attached to human intestinal cells, intracellular uptake was limited. This suggests that human-to-animal transmission is more likely than animal-to-human transmission and that viral uptake likely presents a species barrier.

papers.title: Treatment With Ruxolitinib and TAK-779 Enhances GII.17 Human Norovirus Replication and Enables Serial Passaging in Human Intestinal Enteroids.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Human norovirus (HuNoV) is a major cause of acute viral gastroenteritis. Although it can be replicated in vitro using human intestinal enteroids (HIEs), generating high‐titer viral laboratory stocks remains challenging due to low infection and passage efficiencies. Interferon response and chemokine signaling may be key host pathways that restrict efficient HuNoV replication. Here, we evaluated the effect of their inhibitors, ruxolitinib—a Janus kinase (JAK) 1/JAK2 inhibitor—and TAK‐779—a C‐X‐C motif chemokine receptor 3 (CXCR3)/C‐C motif chemokine receptor (CCR) 5/CCR2 antagonist—on HuNoV replication in wild‐type jejunal HIEs. TAK‐779 increased GII.17 HuNoV replication by 2.3‐ and 6.0‐fold at 48 and 96 h postinfection (hpi), respectively, compared with the DMSO‐treated control. In contrast, ruxolitinib alone did not affect viral replication. Notably, simultaneous treatment with these compounds further enhanced GII.17 replication by 6.0‐ and 10.7‐fold at 48 and 96 hpi, respectively, which enabled serial passaging. These findings imply that the simultaneous suppression of these pathways potentially benefits GII.17 HuNoV replication.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 人类 诺如病毒 (HuNoV) 是急性病毒性胃肠炎的主要原因,但由于使用人肠类肠 (HIE) 的体外感染和传代效率较低,产生高滴度病毒实验室库存仍然具有挑战性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究评估了 ruxolitinib 和 TAK-779 对野生型空肠人肠类中 HuNoV 复制的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 研究人员评估了 ruxolitinib(一种 Janus 激酶 (JAK) 1/JAK2 抑制剂)和 TAK-779(一种 C-X-C 基序趋化因子受体 3 (CXCR3)/C-C 基序趋化因子受体 (CCR) 5/CCR2 拮抗剂)对野生型空肠 HIE 中 HuNoV 复制的影响。
elements_zh.main_results: 与 DMSO 处理的对照相比,TAK-779 在感染后 48 小时和 96 小时分别使 GII.17 HuNoV 复制增加 2.3 倍和 6.0 倍,而单独使用鲁索替尼并不影响病毒复制。治疗 与两种化合物同时使用,在感染后 48 小时和 96 小时分别进一步增强 GII.17 复制 6.0 倍和 10.7 倍,从而实现连续传代。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,同时抑制干扰素反应和趋化因子信号通路可能有利于 GII.17 HuNoV 复制,联合 治疗 实现的增强复制和连续传代就证明了这一点。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,针对特定的 宿主 途径可以改善 GII.17 HuNoV 的体外培养,促进对该待研究菌株的研究,并可能有助于 抗病毒药物 策略的开发。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是在体外使用人肠肠类进行的,可能无法完全重现体内条件;然而,由于复制增强和连续传代的直接观察,证据强度很高。

papers.title: Foodborne outbreak of norovirus GII.17 due to water contamination caused by backflow from a malfunctioning sewage tank.
papers.abstract: Food poisoning caused by human norovirus genotype GII.17 affecting 73 individuals occurred in a single commercial building in Sapporo, Hokkaido, Japan, from late December 2024 to early January 2025. An epidemiological and environmental investigation was carried out and it was identified that the potable water contaminated with the virus was the sole factor for patients with gastrointestinal symptoms. Furthermore, it was revealed that the building's water distribution system was tainted with the virus because the potable water storage tank for supply in the building's underground system was contaminated by sewage which flowed from the wastewater tank. A malfunction of the tank drainage system caused an overflow of sewage containing norovirus into the potable water storage tank, contaminating the building's water supply. Although the mechanism causing this norovirus outbreak is infrequent, ageing building water infrastructure may increase such risks in future, unless appropriate maintenance is regularly performed.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates a norovirus GII.17 outbreak affecting 73 individuals in a commercial building in Sapporo, Japan, from late December 2024 to early January 2025. Through epidemiological and environmental investigation, the outbreak was traced to potable water contamination caused by backflow from a malfunctioning sewage tank into the building's water storage system. The findings highlight an infrequent but critical environmental pathway for norovirus transmission, underscoring the risks of ageing water infrastructure and the need for regular maintenance to prevent future outbreaks. The study provides direct evidence of waterborne norovirus transmission due to infrastructure failure, offering valuable insights for public health surveillance and prevention strategies.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the public-health concern that norovirus incidence in England rose during 2022–2025 while the dominant genotype shifted from GII.4 to GII.17, raising questions about whether genotype changes altered disease severity.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The authors conducted a national observational study using linked laboratory-confirmed norovirus cases and death records in England from 2022 to 2025.
analysis.methods: The study linked norovirus test results with fatality data and assessed associations between case-fatality risk and age, care setting, and genotype using national surveillance datasets.
analysis.main_results: Age and care setting, but not genotype, were associated with case-fatality risk during the study period.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as indicating that host factors and care environment, rather than viral genotype, drove fatal outcomes, highlighting a shift in genotype dominance without a corresponding change in severity.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results suggest that surveillance and prevention strategies should prioritize high-risk groups and care settings rather than focus on genotype monitoring alone.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s observational design and reliance on routine surveillance data limit causal inference and may under-ascertain milder cases, warranting cautious interpretation of the evidence strength as moderate.

analysis.summary_en: This national observational study in England (2022–2025) examined why norovirus incidence rose while the dominant genotype changed from GII.4 to GII.17. Using linked laboratory and fatality records, the authors found that age and care setting, but not genotype, were associated with case-fatality risk. They concluded that host and setting factors, rather than viral genotype, drove fatal outcomes, indicating that surveillance and prevention should prioritize high-risk groups and care environments. The study’s reliance on routine surveillance data and observational design limit causal inference, so the evidence strength is moderate.

papers.title: Clinical Experience of Oral Serum-Derived Bovine Immunoglobulin in Solid Organ Transplant Recipients Diagnosed With Norovirus Infection.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Norovirus gastroenteritis can cause serious complications in solid organ transplant (SOT) recipients, and no licensed treatment is available. Typical therapy is supportive care; however, some medications may be used off-label. Serum-derived bovine immunoglobulin (IG), a medical food product, has been utilized off-label for norovirus gastroenteritis, although clinical efficacy is uncertain. The objective of this study was to evaluate the outcomes of SOT recipients who received serum-derived bovine IG for the treatment of norovirus. METHODS: Adult SOT recipients, who received serum-derived bovine IG as treatment for norovirus between January 2020 and December 2024, were evaluated for inclusion. Outcomes evaluated included improvement in the number of bowel movements to less than three per day, presence of more formed bowel movements, presence of acute kidney injury (AKI), initial response rates, and 90-day relapse-free rate. RESULTS: 14 SOT recipients were included. Nine patients had a history of prior norovirus gastroenteritis. Reduction to less than three bowel movements per day occurred in 8/14 (57%) patients. Overall, 12/14 (86%) patients experienced clinical improvement after a median of 4.5 days of serum-derived bovine IG. Of those alive at 90-day follow-up, 8 of 10 (80%) did not experience relapsing norovirus infection. CONCLUSION: Orally administered serum-derived bovine IG may be a potential option for SOT recipients with chronic norovirus infection. Larger, well-designed studies are needed to further define its clinical efficacy.

papers.title_zh: 口服血清源牛免疫球蛋白在诊断为 诺如病毒 感染的实体器官移植受者中的临床经验。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Norovirus gastroenteritis can cause serious complications in solid organ transplant (SOT) recipients, and no licensed treatment is available. Typical therapy is supportive care; however, some medications may be used off-label. Serum-derived bovine immunoglobulin (IG), a medical food product, has been utilized off-label for norovirus gastroenteritis, although clinical efficacy is uncertain. The objective of this study was to evaluate the outcomes of SOT recipients who received serum-derived bovine IG for the treatment of norovirus. METHODS: Adult SOT recipients, who received serum-derived bovine IG as treatment for norovirus between January 2020 and December 2024, were evaluated for inclusion. Outcomes evaluated included improvement in the number of bowel movements to less than three per day, presence of more formed bowel movements, presence of acute kidney injury (AKI), initial response rates, and 90-day relapse-free rate. RESULTS: 14 SOT recipients were included. Nine patients had a history of prior norovirus gastroenteritis. Reduction to less than three bowel movements per day occurred in 8/14 (57%) patients. Overall, 12/14 (86%) patients experienced clinical improvement after a median of 4.5 days of serum-derived bovine IG. Of those alive at 90-day follow-up, 8 of 10 (80%) did not experience relapsing norovirus infection. CONCLUSION: Orally administered serum-derived bovine IG may be a potential option for SOT recipients with chronic norovirus infection. Larger, well-designed studies are needed to further define its clinical efficacy.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:诺如病毒 胃肠炎可导致实体器官移植(SOT)受者出现严重并发症,且尚无获得许可的 治疗。典型的治疗是支持治疗;然而,某些药物可能会在标签外使用。血清源性牛免疫球蛋白 (IG) 是一种医疗食品,已在标签外用于治疗 诺如病毒 胃肠炎,但临床疗效尚不确定。本研究的目的是评估接受 治疗 或 诺如病毒 血清来源牛 IG 的 SOT 受者的结果。方法:对在 2020 年 1 月至 2024 年 12 月期间接受血清衍生牛 IG 作为 治疗 的成人 SOT 接受者进行纳入评估。评估的结果包括将排便次数改善至每天少于 3 次、排便次数增多、出现急性肾损伤 (AKI)、初始缓解率和 90 天无复发率。结果:包括 14 名 SOT 接受者。九名患者既往有 诺如病毒 胃肠炎病史。8/14 (57%) 的患者每天排便次数减少至少于 3 次。总体而言,12/14 (86%) 的患者在使用血清牛 IG 治疗平均 4.5 天后出现临床改善。在 90 天随访时存活的患者中,10 人中有 8 人 (80%) 没有经历复发性 诺如病毒 感染。结论:对于患有慢性 诺如病毒 感染的 SOT 接受者来说,口服血清源性牛 IG 可能是一个潜在的选择。需要更大规模、精心设计的研究来进一步确定其临床疗效。

papers.title: Subzero Control of Human Norovirus and Indicator Microorganisms on Frozen Foods Using an Antifreeze–Peracetic Acid Formulation
papers.abstract: Human norovirus (HuNoV) is one of the most important foodborne viruses and poses a significant risk in frozen foods along the cold chain. Traditional disinfectants exhibit reduced efficacy in frozen matrices and often fail to meet the requirements for food applications. This study optimized and evaluated a novel antifreeze–peracetic acid formulation (Af-PAA) for application on frozen foods, achieving disinfection performance at −40 °C. The formulation was optimized using four indicator microorganisms, with effective Af-PAA concentrations of 200 mg/L for Escherichia coli, 200 mg/L for Staphylococcus aureus, 500 mg/L for Candida albicans, and 2000 mg/L for Aspergillus niger. HuNoV GII.4[P31] propagated in zebrafish was inoculated onto frozen food samples. The frozen blueberries (500 mg/L), carrots (500 mg/L), chicken breast (2000 mg/L), and Arctic shrimp (2000 mg/L) were then subjected to Af-PAA treatment at −40 °C for 60 min with 60 s vortex mixing. RNase-RT-qPCR analysis showed a 3.0–3.1 log10 reduction in RNase-resistant HuNoV RNA signals across all tested food under the corresponding treatment concentrations. No visual changes were observed in treated foods. This study demonstrated that Af-PAA met tested food disinfectant requirements and effectively inactivated indicator microorganisms. HuNoV signals were also markedly reduced on the tested foods. These findings support its application for microbial risk control in cold-chain foods.

papers.title: Aggregation of Tulane Virus, a Human Norovirus Surrogate, Under Various Ionic Conditions: Implications in Thermal Tolerance
papers.abstract: Abstract Human norovirus is a major cause of foodborne illness worldwide, and the lack of a reliable cell culture system limits direct studies. Tulane virus has been used as a robust culturable human norovirus surrogate with similar capsid and genome structures; however, little is known about its particle size and zeta potential under varying ionic strengths and pH conditions, factors which are critical for understanding virus adsorption in food and environmental matrices and its fate when present in aggregated versus dispersed forms. This study investigated Tulane virus aggregation, zeta potential, and whether aggregation impacts virus thermal tolerance. Dynamic light scattering showed aggregation in 1 mM (pH 4.5) and 10 mM calcium chloride (pH 4.5–6.3), whereas 100 mM calcium chloride induced aggregation across a broader pH range (3.3–10), with all aggregation conditions occurring net surface charge approaches zero. Aggregation reduced countable infectious viral particles by ∼4 log10 PFU per ml, dependent upon aggregates size and number. Thermal tolerance of virus aggregates when held at 60 °C for 2 min was not significantly different from that of dispersed particles. These results indicate that the virus will readily aggregate under ionic conditions typical of food and environmental systems, providing important insights into the adsorption and stability of human norovirus surrogates.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human norovirus is a major cause of foodborne illness globally, and the lack of a reliable cell culture system limits direct studies. This study aimed to investigate how ionic conditions affect Tulane virus aggregation and its thermal tolerance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in a laboratory setting to examine Tulane virus aggregation under various ionic conditions. It involved testing different concentrations of calcium chloride and varying pH levels to observe the effects on virus behavior.
analysis.methods: Dynamic light scattering was used to measure virus aggregation, zeta potential, and thermal tolerance under different ionic strengths and pH conditions. The study also assessed the impact of aggregation on the countable infectious viral particles.
analysis.main_results: Dynamic light scattering showed that aggregation occurred in 1 mM (pH 4.5) and 10 mM calcium chloride (pH 4.5–6.3), whereas 100 mM calcium chloride induced aggregation across a broader pH range (3.3–10), with all aggregation conditions occurring when net surface charge approached zero. Aggregation reduced countable infectious viral particles by ∼4 log10 PFU per ml, dependent upon aggregates size and number.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that Tulane virus readily aggregates under ionic conditions typical of food and environmental systems, providing important insights into the adsorption and stability of human norovirus surrogates.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results can inform the understanding of norovirus behavior in food and environmental matrices, which is critical for improving surveillance, diagnosis, and risk assessment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited to laboratory conditions and did not account for real-world environmental variability. The evidence is moderate as it is based on in vitro experiments and does not include field data.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated how ionic conditions affect the aggregation and thermal tolerance of Tulane virus, a human norovirus surrogate. The research aimed to address the limitations in studying human noroviruses due to the lack of a reliable cell culture system. Dynamic light scattering revealed that aggregation occurs under specific ionic strengths and pH levels, with the extent of aggregation influencing the countable infectious viral particles. The results indicate that Tulane virus readily aggregates in conditions typical of food and environmental systems, offering insights into norovirus adsorption and stability. However, the study was limited to in vitro experiments, which may not fully represent real-world scenarios. The findings have moderate scientific significance for understanding norovirus behavior in environmental matrices, but they do not directly inform public health interventions or policies.

papers.title_zh: 杜兰病毒(人类 诺如病毒 替代品)在各种离子条件下的聚集:对热耐受性的影响
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Human norovirus is a major cause of foodborne illness worldwide, and the lack of a reliable cell culture system limits direct studies. Tulane virus has been used as a robust culturable human norovirus surrogate with similar capsid and genome structures; however, little is known about its particle size and zeta potential under varying ionic strengths and pH conditions, factors which are critical for understanding virus adsorption in food and environmental matrices and its fate when present in aggregated versus dispersed forms. This study investigated Tulane virus aggregation, zeta potential, and whether aggregation impacts virus thermal tolerance. Dynamic light scattering showed aggregation in 1 mM (pH 4.5) and 10 mM calcium chloride (pH 4.5–6.3), whereas 100 mM calcium chloride induced aggregation across a broader pH range (3.3–10), with all aggregation conditions occurring net surface charge approaches zero. Aggregation reduced countable infectious viral particles by ∼4 log10 PFU per ml, dependent upon aggregates size and number. Thermal tolerance of virus aggregates when held at 60 °C for 2 min was not significantly different from that of dispersed particles. These results indicate that the virus will readily aggregate under ionic conditions typical of food and environmental systems, providing important insights into the adsorption and stability of human norovirus surrogates.

papers.full_text: Page 290 SURVEILLANCE CCDR • July/August 2026 • Vol. 52 No. 7/8 Wastewater surveillance as an early warning indicator for norovirus: Validating wastewater signals against clinical indicators in British Columbia, Canada, 2021–2025 Bridget Irwin1,2*, Natalie Prystajecky2,3, Mayank Singal2,4, Sharon Relova2, Anya Smith2, David McVea2,4 Abstract Background: Norovirus is the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis globally and causes significant morbidity. Despite this, norovirus is not reportable to the public health system in most jurisdictions, making it challenging to detect and control local transmission. Wastewater- based epidemiology is a potential tool for narrowing this gap, allowing for non-invasive, population-level surveillance. Objective: In this study, it assess wastewater-based epidemiology as a surveillance tool for monitoring norovirus in British Columbia, Canada, by comparing norovirus wastewater signals to norovirus-related hospital admissions and genogroup I (GI)-related emergency department (ED) visits. Methods: More than six thousand (n=6,167) wastewater samples from 12 municipal treatment plants were collected between January 10, 2021–September 27, 2025 and pooled to generate a population-weighted average for the province. Norovirus hospital admissions and GI-related ED visits were extracted for the same period from the Discharge Abstract Database and the National Ambulatory Care Reporting System, respectively, and were compared with wastewater signals using time-lagged cross-correlation analyses. Results: Time-lagged cross-correlation analyses indicate significant positive correlation overall between unadjusted norovirus wastewater concentrations and norovirus hospitalizations (Spearman’s ρ=0.69, p<0.01) and GI-related ED visits (Spearman’s ρ=0.84, p<0.01), with wastewater leading hospitalizations by two weeks (Spearman’s ρ=0.71) and aligned with ED visits (Spearman’s ρ=0.83). Conclusion: The findings support the validity of using wastewater-based epidemiology for monitoring norovirus at the population-level and suggest that it may provide an early warning signal for severe norovirus activity requiring hospitalization, prompting a more timely response. Introduction Norovirus is the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide and causes significant illness (1,2), estimated at over 677 million cases globally per year (1,2), including over three million in Canada (3). Spread through fecal-oral or vomit-oral routes, norovirus presents with rapid onset of nausea, vomiting and diarrhea and is highly infectious, with fewer than 100 viral SURVEILLANCE Page 291 CCDR • July/August 2026 • Vol. 52 No. 7/8 particles required to cause illness (4). This low infectious dose, combined with extended and asymptomatic viral shedding, short-lived immunity and strong environmental persistence, results in efficient transmission and frequent outbreaks (4). While most norovirus cases resolve within one to two days with supportive treatment, young children, the elderly and people with medical co-morbidities may develop complications resulting in hospitalization or death (4,5). Globally, norovirus is estimated to cause over 200,000 deaths and to cost $60.3 billion USD each year (over $80 billion CAD) due to healthcare costs and productivity losses (2,6). In Canada, hospitalization costs are estimated to exceed $21 million CAD (7). Despite its health and economic impacts, norovirus is not considered a disease of public health significance in most jurisdictions, including in British Columbia (BC), Canada, where reporting is only required for facility-based outbreaks and laboratory confirmation is not mandatory. Although the national incidence of laboratory confirmed norovirus cases is collected and reported weekly by the National Enteric Surveillance Program, a 2014 to 2015 study found that just 14.5% of Canadians experiencing acute gastroenteritis sought medical care, and only 12.5% of those were ordered to undergo diagnostic testing (8). This low rate of health care seeking and testing means that the disease is systematically underrepresented in surveillance databases and its true burden is difficult to assess. Wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) gained prominence during the COVID-19 pandemic as a valuable public health surveillance tool, particularly in situations where clinical testing is limited. Wastewater-based epidemiology involves extracting viral information from fecal matter and offers several benefits over traditional surveillance, including that it provides a non-invasive, population level estimate of disease prevalence (9–12) and that it captures both symptomatic and asymptomatic infections (11,13). Wastewater-based epidemiology may also have economic benefits and has been shown to be more cost-effective than clinical surveillance in some settings, particularly those with high disease severity, minimal routine clinical surveillance and high intervention effectiveness (11,14,15). Furthermore, there is evidence to suggest that WBE can detect some viruses prior to symptom onset. This may allow it to be used to predict disease activity in the community and guide interventions, though the extent of this lead time varies across temporal and geographic contexts (10,11,13,16,17). Given its success for COVID-19, WBE is increasingly being adapted to monitor other pathogens such as norovirus. Indeed, WBE has the potential to improve norovirus surveillance by allowing for routine monitoring of the burden of illness and temporal trends in the community, as well as providing valuable information on the emergence of new outbreaks and variants of the disease. Such information can guide public health actions to reduce transmission and may also provide an early warning to healthcare facilities, supporting preparedness efforts and the implementation of preventative measures. Wastewater-based epidemiology for norovirus has been explored globally (18–29) and several studies have found that wastewater signals correlate relatively well with both outbreak counts (18,29–31) and individual case counts (21,23,31,32); however, few researchers have investigated long term trends in these relationships and little work has been done to explore WBE as an early warning indicator. Given these gaps and building on previous work, this study seeks to evaluate WBE as a tool for monitoring severe norovirus in BC by assessing correlation between norovirus concentrations in wastewater and clinical indicators over a multi-year period. Methods Wastewater sample collection and processing Between January 10, 2021 and September 27, 2025, influent wastewater samples were collected one to five times per week from 12 predominantly urban wastewater treatment plants (WWTPs) across BC. Combined, these facilities treat the waste of approximately 57% of the population (3.2 million people), including the majority of Metro Vancouver. At each treatment plant, 24-hour composite samples were collected using autosamplers and one litre of coarsely screened raw influent was extracted. Samples were refrigerated prior to shipping and were transported in coolers on ice to the BC Centre for Disease Control laboratory within 48 hours of collection for immediate processing. Wastewater processing methods are described in full in Appendix, Supplemental material. Briefly, samples were homogenized and concentrated by centrifugal filtration before being subjected to automated RNA extraction. Extracted ribonucleic acid (RNA) was tested for the presence of genogroup I (GI) and genogroup II (GII) norovirus using multi- plex real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR), with a spiked in synthetic DNA used as an inhibition control. A standard curve generated with synthetic DNA was used to quantify norovirus in the samples. Assays demonstrated high linearity with a lower limit of detection of cycle threshold (CT) 35, and viral concentrations were calculated as genome copies per millilitre of wastewater using RT-qPCR results and sample-specific conversion factors. Clinical data Hospitalization data for BC residents were extracted from the Discharge Abstract Database (DAD) for the time period, January 10, 2021 to September 27, 2025. All 81 acute care facilities in BC must report to the DAD, which captures up to 25 diagnoses per admission using International Classification of Diseases, 10th revision, Canada (ICD-10-CA) codes (33). Cases were included in this study if a diagnosis of acute gastroenteropathy due to norovirus (ICD-10-CA code A08.1) Page 292 SURVEILLANCE CCDR • July/August 2026 • Vol. 52 No. 7/8 was recorded in any position. Emergency department (ED) visit data for BC residents were extracted for the 30 BC EDs included in the National Ambulatory Care Reporting System (NACRS) during the same time period. The NACRS includes data on approximately 76.4% of all provincial ED visits and captures up to three complaints per visit using Canadian Emergency Department Information System (CEDIS) codes (34). Cases were included in this study if a presenting complaint of diarrhea (CEDIS code 254) or nausea and/or vomiting (CEDIS code 257) was recorded in any position. Statistical analyses Statistical analyses and data visualizations were performed using R Studio version 2023.06.1 (35). For ease of comparison, clinical and wastewater data were down sampled to a single measurement for each epidemiological week of the study to create an evenly spaced dataset with 246 observations. For hospitalizations and ED visits, cases were summed per epidemiological week of presentation. For the wastewater samples, viral concentrations of GI and GII were summed to determine the overall norovirus load and the resulting values were normalized by the WWTP’s daily flow rate to adjust for variation in day-to-day wastewater volume using the following formula: virus copies per litre × flow in litres per day = virus copies per day Weekly weighted average norovirus concentrations were then calculated to account for WWTPs serving different percentages of the population and sampling occurring at different frequencies, as described in Appendix, Supplemental material. The data were not normally distributed, so non-parametric measures of analysis were used. First, crude correlation between norovirus wastewater concentrations and clinical indicators was assessed using Spearman’s rho coefficient (ρ) (36). Next, time lagged cross-correlations were calculated to determine at what shift peak synchrony occurred between the wastewater concentrations and the clinical indicators. Positive time lagged cross-correlation lag times indicated that wastewater signals preceded the clinical indicators, while negative lag times indicated that wastewater signals lagged the clinical indicators (37,38). Time lagged cross-correlations were generated using the ccf_boot function in the R package “funtimes” (37), which accounts for potential autocorrelation in wastewater concentrations and clinical indicators by repeatedly resampling the data to ensure the results are reliable (37,39). All analyses were performed both on the unadjusted wastewater data and on wastewater data normalized for flow. Locally estimated scatterplot smoothing with a span of 0.02 was applied to both the wastewater and clinical timeseries data to reduce short-term noise while preserving overall trends. Results A total of 6,167 influent wastewater samples were collected over the study period, of which 94.3% were positive for norovirus GI and 99.9% were positive for norovirus GII. During the same period, there were 1,252 hospital admissions related to norovirus (ranging from 0–24 admissions per week), where norovirus was the most responsible diagnosis for 46.3% (median position=2; interquartile range [IQR]: 3) and 237,365 ED visits related to GI symptoms (ranging from 595–1,502 visits per week), where diarrhea or nausea/vomiting was the primary presenting complaint for 93.4% (median position=1; IQR: 0). The ages of the individuals admitted to hospital and presenting to the ED are summarized in Table 1. Hospitalizations were a mean of 63.04 years (± 27.36), while ED visits were a mean of 35.98 years (± 27.38). Table 1: Age characteristics of norovirus-related hospital admissions and gastrointestinal-related emergency department visits in British Columbia, 2021–2025 Age group (years) Hospital admissions n (%) Emergency department visits n (%) 0–4 61 (4.87%) 42,329 (17.83%) 5–11 49 (3.91%) 20,390 (8.59%) 12–18 34 (2.72%) 11,800 (4.97%) 19–29 45 (3.59%) 36,014 (15.17%) 30–39 70 (5.59%) 29,320 (8.59%) 40–49 51 (4.07%) 19,827 (8.35%) 50–59 88 (7.03%) 19,545 (8.23%) 60–69 177 (14.14%) 21,005 (8.85%) 70–79 233 (18.61%) 19,276 (8.12%) 80 and older 421 (33.63%) 17,840 (7.52%) Unknown 23 (1.84%) 19 (0.01%) Total 1,252 237,365 Overall, trends in norovirus wastewater mirrored hospitalizations and ED visits, with wastewater and clinical indicators highest in the winter and spring each year and lowest in the summer and fall for both unadjusted (Figure 1, Figure 2) and flow-normalized (Figure 1, Figure 2) wastewater. Crude correlation analyses showed moderate-strong positive correlation between norovirus concentrations and hospitalizations (Spearman’s ρ=0.69; p<0.001) and ED visits (Spearman’s ρ=0.84; p<0.001), and these findings held when wastewater was normalized for flow (hospitalizations: Spearman’s ρ=0.62; p<0.001; ED visits: Spearman’s ρ=0.76; p<0.001). SURVEILLANCE Page 293 CCDR • July/August 2026 • Vol. 52 No. 7/8 Time lagged cross-correlation analyses were performed to assess the temporal relationships between wastewater concentrations and hospitalizations (Figure 3) and ED visits (Figure 4). The strongest correlation between the wastewater signal and hospital admissions occurred when wastewater preceded admissions by two weeks (unadjusted wastewater: peak synchrony=2, Spearman’s ρ=0.71; flow-normalized wastewater: peak synchrony=2, Spearman’s ρ=0.64). The strongest correlation between the wastewater signal and ED visits occurred when the signals were not shifted (unadjusted wastewater: peak synchrony=0, Spearman’s ρ=0.83), or when wastewater lagged ED visits by one week (adjusted wastewater: peak synchrony=−1, Spearman’s ρ=0.76). Discussion This study evaluated the validity of WBE as a surveillance tool for monitoring norovirus in BC by comparing wastewater concentrations to hospital admissions and ED visits over a 4.75-year period. While clinical indicators underestimate true disease burden and are an imperfect comparator, wastewater signals correlate with well with both hospital admissions and ED visits. This indicates that norovirus levels in wastewater reflect real-world illness trends and may serve as a valid proxy for disease incidence where individual cases are not reportable. This is consistent with the findings of previous research and adds to the evidence supporting the use of WBE for norovirus surveillance (18–32). Time lagged cross-correlations showed that increases in wastewater signals preceded increases in norovirus-related hospital admissions by approximately two weeks, suggesting that wastewater may provide an early warning of severe norovirus disease. This may afford healthcare facilities critical lead time to consider resource allocation and implement strategies to prevent further transmission, such as enhanced screening and cleaning protocols. Conversely, the highest correlation between wastewater signals and ED visits occurred when neither was shifted (unadjusted wastewater) or when ED visits preceded wastewater by one week, indicating that both occur around the same time, with wastewater signals potentially lagging ED visits. analysis.research_question_and_background: Norovirus is the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis globally and causes significant morbidity, but it is not reportable to the public health system in most jurisdictions, making it challenging to detect and control local transmission.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study was conducted in British Columbia, Canada, from January 10, 2021, to September 27, 2025, using wastewater samples from 12 municipal treatment plants and comparing them with norovirus-related hospital admissions and genogroup I (GI)-related emergency department visits.
analysis.methods: More than six thousand (n=6,167) wastewater samples were collected and pooled to generate a population-weighted average for the province, while norovirus hospital admissions and GI-related ED visits were extracted from the Discharge Abstract Database and the National Ambulatory Care Reporting System, respectively, and compared using time-lagged cross-correlation analyses.
analysis.main_results: Time-lagged cross-correlation analyses indicate significant positive correlation between unadjusted norovirus wastewater concentrations and norovirus hospitalizations (Spearman's ρ=0.69, p<0.01) and GI-related ED visits (Spearman's ρ=0.84, p<0.01), with wastewater leading hospitalizations by two weeks and aligned with ED visits.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings support the validity of using wastewater-based epidemiology for monitoring norovirus at the population-level and suggest that it may provide an early warning signal for severe norovirus activity requiring hospitalization, prompting a more timely response.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Wastewater surveillance can serve as an early warning indicator for norovirus, enabling more timely public health responses and improving the detection and control of local transmission, particularly in jurisdictions where norovirus is not reportable.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is high due to the large sample size and significant statistical correlations, though limitations may include potential confounding factors in wastewater sampling and clinical data collection.

analysis.summary_en: This study validates wastewater surveillance as an early warning indicator for norovirus in British Columbia, Canada, from 2021 to 2025. By analyzing over 6,000 wastewater samples and comparing them with clinical data, researchers found significant positive correlations between wastewater signals and hospitalizations (ρ=0.69, p<0.01) and emergency department visits (ρ=0.84, p<0.01), with wastewater leading hospitalizations by two weeks. The findings support wastewater-based epidemiology as a valuable tool for population-level norovirus monitoring, potentially enabling earlier public health interventions. This approach addresses the challenge of detecting norovirus in jurisdictions where it is not reportable, offering a non-invasive method for surveillance.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 诺如病毒 是全球 急性胃肠炎 的主要原因,并导致严重发病,但大多数司法管辖区并未向公共卫生系统报告,这使得检测和控制当地 传播 具有挑战性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究于 2021 年 1 月 10 日至 2025 年 9 月 27 日在加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚省进行,使用了 12 个市政 治疗 工厂的废水样本,并将其与 诺如病毒 相关的住院情况和基因组 I (GI) 相关的急诊就诊进行了比较。
elements_zh.methods: 收集并汇总了六千多个(n = 6,167)废水样本,以生成该省的人口加权平均值,同时分别从出院摘要数据库和国家门诊护理报告系统中提取 诺如病毒 住院情况和胃肠道相关急诊就诊情况,并使用时滞互相关分析进行比较。
elements_zh.main_results: 时滞互相关分析表明,未调整的 诺如病毒 废水浓度与 诺如病毒 住院率 (Spearman's ρ=0.69,p<0.01) 和胃肠道相关急诊就诊率 (Spearman's ρ=0.84,p<0.01) 之间存在显着正相关性,废水导致住院率领先两周,并且与急诊就诊率一致。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: Norovirus is the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis globally and causes significant morbidity, but it is not reportable to the public health system in most jurisdictions, making it challenging to detect and control local transmission.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This study was conducted in British Columbia, Canada, from January 10, 2021, to September 27, 2025, using wastewater samples from 12 municipal treatment plants and comparing them with norovirus-related hospital admissions and genogroup I (GI)-related emergency department visits.
analysis_en.methods: More than six thousand (n=6,167) wastewater samples were collected and pooled to generate a population-weighted average for the province, while norovirus hospital admissions and GI-related ED visits were extracted from the Discharge Abstract Database and the National Ambulatory Care Reporting System, respectively, and compared using time-lagged cross-correlation analyses.
analysis_en.main_results: Time-lagged cross-correlation analyses indicate significant positive correlation between unadjusted norovirus wastewater concentrations and norovirus hospitalizations (Spearman's ρ=0.69, p<0.01) and GI-related ED visits (Spearman's ρ=0.84, p<0.01), with wastewater leading hospitalizations by two weeks and aligned with ED visits.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings support the validity of using wastewater-based epidemiology for monitoring norovirus at the population-level and suggest that it may provide an early warning signal for severe norovirus activity requiring hospitalization, prompting a more timely response.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Wastewater surveillance can serve as an early warning indicator for norovirus, enabling more timely public health responses and improving the detection and control of local transmission, particularly in jurisdictions where norovirus is not reportable.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence strength is high due to the large sample size and significant statistical correlations, though limitations may include potential confounding factors in wastewater sampling and clinical data collection.

papers.title: Human-Associated Viral Pathogens in Water and Air and Evaluation of PMMoV as an Indicator of Airborne Viruses near the Tijuana River, CA.
papers.abstract: Coastal waters impacted by fecal contamination pose health risks to recreational users through direct water contact; however, risk to users, workers and surrounding communities from potential airborne exposure remain poorly understood. This study quantified two human-associated sewage markers (HF183 and pepper mild mottle virus (PMMoV)) and two enteric viruses (norovirus GII (NoVGII) and human adenovirus (HAdV)) in paired water and air samples collected in San Diego County, USA, from the Tijuana River, a binational river flowing into the US from Mexico that is polluted with untreated and treated wastewater, a community site on the beach (Imperial Beach), and a northern reference site (La Jolla Shores). A total of 23 paired water and air samples were collected during the dry season, with 10 water samples collected during the wet season. All microbial targets were consistently detected at high concentrations in the Tijuana River water, while concentrations in Imperial Beach water were significantly lower. In contrast, airborne concentrations were comparable between the two sites, with PMMoV detected in all air samples. Log-transformed ratios of the concentrations in air and water samples indicate enrichment in the air samples from Imperial Beach compared to the Tijuana River. PMMoV showed the most consistent detection and the strongest relationship with airborne HAdV and NoV levels, suggesting PMMoV as a conservative indicator of aerosolized viruses of human fecal origin in such settings. These findings indicate that coastal surf zones may serve as important interfaces for aerosolization of wastewater-associated microorganisms and suggest that inhalation could represent a previously underrecognized exposure pathway in contaminated coastal environments.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the poorly understood health risks from airborne exposure to human-associated viruses in coastal areas impacted by fecal contamination, specifically evaluating whether inhalation could be an underrecognized exposure pathway near wastewater-polluted surf zones.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study collected paired water and air samples from three sites in San Diego County, USA: the Tijuana River, Imperial Beach, and La Jolla Shores, with 23 paired samples during the dry season and 10 water samples during the wet season.
analysis.methods: Microbial targets included two human-associated sewage markers (HF183 and PMMoV) and two enteric viruses (NoVGII and HAdV), with concentrations measured in paired water and air samples to assess aerosolization.
analysis.main_results: All microbial targets were consistently detected at high concentrations in the Tijuana River water, while concentrations in Imperial Beach water were significantly lower; airborne concentrations were comparable between the two sites, and PMMoV was detected in all air samples.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that coastal surf zones may serve as important interfaces for aerosolization of wastewater-associated microorganisms and proposed PMMoV as a conservative indicator of aerosolized viruses of human fecal origin in such settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings suggest that inhalation could represent a previously underrecognized exposure pathway in contaminated coastal environments, informing future surveillance and risk assessment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was limited by a small sample size and a focus on a single geographic region, which may constrain generalizability; the evidence strength is moderate due to the observational design and lack of direct health outcome data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究解决了受粪便污染影响的沿海地区空气传播人类相关病毒所带来的健康风险知之甚少的问题,特别评估了吸入是否可能是废水污染冲浪区附近未被充分认识的暴露途径。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究从美国圣地亚哥县蒂华纳河、帝国海滩和拉霍亚海岸三个地点采集了配对的水和空气样本,其中旱季有 23 个配对样本,雨季有 10 个水样本。
elements_zh.methods: 微生物目标包括两种与人类相关的污水标记物(HF183和PMMoV)和两种肠道病毒(NoVGII和HAdV),在配对的水和空气样本中测量浓度以评估气溶胶。
elements_zh.main_results: 所有微生物目标在蒂华纳河水中均检测到高浓度,而帝国海滩水中的浓度明显较低;两个地点的空气传播浓度相当,所有空气样本中均检测到 PMMoV。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,沿海冲浪区可能是废水相关微生物雾化的重要界面,并提出 PMMoV 作为此类环境中人类粪便来源的雾化病毒的保守指标。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现表明,吸入可能代表了受污染的沿海环境中以前未被充分认识的暴露途径,为未来的 监测 和风险评估策略提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究受到样本量较小且只关注单一地理区域的限制,这可能会限制普遍性;由于观察设计和缺乏直接的健康结果数据,证据强度中等。

papers.title: On the Numerical Solution of the Multiscale Models Characterising Noroviral Infectious Disease Systems Using the Multistage Spectral the Relaxation Method and the Nonstandard Finite Difference Method
papers.abstract: Multiscale models for infectious disease systems are highly nonlinear. This presents substantial difficulties for both analysis and computation. Consequently, there is a continuous demand for the development of efficient numerical methods that provide reliable solutions. Over time, various numerical techniques have been developed for single-scale models. However, multiscale models have increasingly relied on built-in solvers and, more recently, the nonstandard finite difference method. The primary aim of this study is to offer an in-depth examination of the multistage spectral relaxation method (MSRM) applied to the multiscale model characterising norovirus infection. This study also provides a comprehensive comparison with the nonstandard finite difference method (NSFDM) in terms of convergence and accuracy, as well as their handling of highly nonlinear systems of ordinary differential equations. Both schemes were validated against an adaptive ODE45 scheme in MATLAB2025a, which served as the reference solver. The numerical outcomes indicate that the MSRM achieves a better accuracy level, with relative L2 errors ranging from 10−9 to 10−7 for Δτ≤0.10 and Nch=8. In contrast, the NSFDM provides solid first-order accuracy, yielding L2 errors around 10−4, while ensuring strict unconditional positivity and stability across all tested step sizes from h=0.01 to 2.0. This study features a parameter sensitivity analysis that varies βH,δH,αh,μV,μH, as well as semi-log error graphs, convergence rate visuals, and CPU performance benchmarks. The MSRM costs about 24 times more per run, but it offers better accuracy for between-host variables. This makes it the preferred method for high-fidelity applications. In contrast, the NSFDM is the best option for quick parameter sweeps and long simulations that require guaranteed positivity.

papers.abstract_zh: 传染病系统的多尺度模型是高度非线性的。这给分析和计算带来了很大的困难。因此,不断需要开发能够提供可靠解决方案的高效数值方法。随着时间的推移,针对单尺度模型开发了各种数值技术。然而,多尺度模型越来越依赖内置求解器,以及最近的非标准有限差分法。本研究的主要目的是深入研究应用于表征 诺如病毒 感染的多尺度模型的多级谱弛豫方法 (MSRM)。本研究还与非标准有限差分法(NSFDM)在收敛性和精度以及对常微分方程的高度非线性系统的处理方面进行了全面比较。这两种方案都针对 MATLAB2025a 中的自适应 ODE45 方案进行了验证,该方案用作参考求解器。数值结果表明,MSRM 达到了更好的精度水平,对于 Δτ≤0.10 和 Nch=8,相对 L2 误差范围为 10−9 到 10−7。相比之下,NSFDM 提供了可靠的一阶精度,产生大约 10−4 左右的 L2 误差,同时确保从 h=0.01 到 2.0 的所有测试步长的严格无条件正性和稳定性。这项研究的特点是对不同 βH、δH、αh、μV、μH 进行参数敏感性分析,以及半对数误差图、收敛速度视觉效果和 CPU 性能基准。MSRM 每次运行的成本大约高出 24 倍,但它为 宿主 之间的变量提供了更高的准确性。这使其成为高保真应用的首选方法。相比之下,NSFDM 是需要保证正性的快速参数扫描和长时间模拟的最佳选择。

news.content_title: Moderna Norovirus Vaccine Fails Interim Bar: Trial Extends Into Fourth Season
news.content: Moderna's most-delayed vaccine program hit another wall on Thursday. The company disclosed in its Q2 2026 earnings release that mRNA-1403 — its experimental mRNA-based norovirus vaccine — did not meet the pre-specified statistical threshold for early success at a Phase 3 interim analysis, extending a trial that has now stretched across three enrollment seasons, one FDA clinical hold, and a case-accrual collapse on two continents. No approved norovirus vaccine exists anywhere in the world, and Thursday's interim miss does not mean one is coming soon. Shares of Moderna (NASDAQ: MRNA) fell roughly 7% in morning trading on the news, even as the company reported a Q2 net loss of $782 million that was modestly better than the year-ago figure and beat Wall Street's consensus estimate. The stock reaction reflected where investor attention landed: not on the financials, but on the pipeline. What "Missing the Interim Bar" Actually Means — and What It Does Not Before treating Thursday's disclosure as a verdict on mRNA-1403, it is worth being precise about what an interim analysis miss does and does not mean — because the two are often conflated and the distinction matters for the 21 million Americans who contract norovirus every year. A Phase 3 trial with a planned interim analysis is designed to allow early stopping if the evidence of efficacy is so strong that continuing the study would be unnecessary. The statistical threshold for that "early success" determination is intentionally set higher than the threshold for the trial's final readout — because looking at accumulating data multiple times inflates the risk of a false positive, and trial designers account for this by requiring stronger evidence at each interim look. Missing the early-success threshold means the data, at this point in the trial, do not clear that higher bar. It does not mean the data show the vaccine does not work. The trial remains ongoing, blinded, and scientifically sound. Moderna is now adding an additional cohort to generate more cases, and a definitive efficacy readout — held to a lower, more standard statistical bar — will come when sufficient cases have accrued. The company did not disclose the observed efficacy point estimate from the interim analysis, consistent with the blinded study design. Three Seasons, One Hold, and Why Norovirus Makes This So Hard The chronology of the Nova 301 trial illustrates a challenge that predates Moderna and will outlast it: norovirus is one of the most difficult pathogens in the world to run a vaccine efficacy trial against, as documented in epidemiological reviews of the development challenges. Moderna dosed the first participant in September 2024, timing the launch to coincide with the Northern Hemisphere norovirus season — the disease peaks between October and March in the US, Europe, Japan, and Canada. After completing Northern Hemisphere enrollment, the trial relocated to the Southern Hemisphere to track that region's winter season. It ran into a wall. In its Q3 2025 earnings release, Moderna disclosed it was unable to accrue sufficient cases in the south and would need to return to the Northern Hemisphere for a second season, 2025–2026. The trial's trouble was compounded in February 2025, when the FDA placed Nova 301 on clinical hold following a single adverse event report of Guillain-Barré syndrome — a rare neurological condition where the immune system attacks the peripheral nervous system. Moderna said at the time that it did not expect the hold to affect the efficacy readout timeline, since Northern Hemisphere enrollment had already been completed. The FDA lifted the hold approximately in May 2025. The GBS case remains under investigation; a single case in a trial of approximately 25,000 participants does not establish a causal link to the vaccine. What Thursday's interim miss adds is a third failure of the case-accrual process — this time at the statistical threshold level rather than the geographic level. Moderna is now preparing to enroll yet another cohort. The Technical Reason mRNA Cannot Fix This Problem The norovirus trial's struggles highlight a distinction that is easy to miss: the mRNA platform's celebrated speed advantage addresses a manufacturing timeline problem, not a disease-surveillance problem. When TechTimes covered Moderna's mFLUSIVA flu vaccine in June 2026, a central argument for the platform was that mRNA can compress strain selection to final vaccine from six months to two to three months, allowing better matching to late-breaking flu variants. That advantage is real for flu, where the pathogen circulates reliably every winter and the bottleneck is manufacturing speed. Norovirus is different. The pathogen circulates in seasonal waves, but those waves are geographically uneven, year-to-year variable, and driven by outbreak clusters in healthcare settings, schools, military bases, and cruise ships rather than by broad community transmission, as epidemiological research has documented. Designing an mRNA sequence for a norovirus target takes days. Waiting for enough norovirus cases to appear in the vaccinated population — so that researchers can measure whether vaccinated people got sick less often than unvaccinated people — can take years. The mRNA platform does not accelerate that wait. mRNA-1403 is a trivalent vaccine, encoding the major capsid protein (VP1) of three norovirus genotypes — GII.4, GI.3, and GII.3 — encapsulated in lipid nanoparticles, the same delivery system as Moderna's flu and COVID vaccines. Those three genotypes together represent the dominant strains causing norovirus-related acute gastroenteritis globally, as described in Phase 1/2 immunogenicity data published in Open Forum Infectious Diseases. Phase 1/2 data confirmed robust HBGA-blocking antibody responses and Th1-predominant CD4+ T cell responses against all three targets — the immunological profile needed for protection, as detailed in cellular and humoral immunogenicity analyses from the Phase 1/2 trial. The science appears to be working. The epidemiology is the constraint. The Financial Stakes: Cash, Losses, and Why August 5 Matters More Than Ever Moderna reported Q2 2026 total revenue of $145 million, up marginally from $142 million in the same quarter of 2025. Product sales of $94 million declined from $114 million a year ago — lower COVID vaccine shipments to the US and South America — but were offset by deliveries to the UK under a long-term government partnership and higher manufacturing collaboration revenue. The net loss was $782 million, or $1.97 per share, about 5% better than the $825 million loss in Q2 2025. Operating expenses fell across the board: cost of sales dropped 22% to $93 million (including $41 million in inventory write-downs and $23 million in unutilized manufacturing capacity charges); research and development declined 7% to $651 million; and selling, general and administrative costs fell 6% to $216 million. For the first half of 2026, Moderna used $1.16 billion in operating cash — a significant but improving figure compared to the $1.96 billion consumed in the first half of 2025. The cash position at June 30 stood at $6.9 billion in cash, equivalents, and investments. That figure does not reflect a $950 million litigation settlement payment Moderna made in July 2026, announced during Q1 2026. The company now expects year-end 2026 cash and investments of $4.7 to $5.2 billion — an improvement of about $200 million from its prior forecast, reflecting tighter cost management. That year-end cash projection frames the importance of August 5: the FDA's PDUFA goal date for mFLUSIVA (mRNA-1010), Moderna's experimental mRNA flu vaccine. If the FDA approves mFLUSIVA by that date, it would become Moderna's fifth commercial product and its first vaccine against a routine, annually recurring disease — a commercial milestone that analysts have estimated could contribute $1 billion to the company's coffers by 2028. The VRBPAC voted 9–0 on June 18, 2026, to recommend mFLUSIVA for adults 50 and older — a unanimous endorsement the FDA rarely ignores. Moderna reaffirmed its guidance for full-year 2026 revenue growth of up to 10% over 2025. Norovirus: Why the Unmet Need Justifies Continued Investment Moderna's decision to add an additional cohort rather than abandon the program is a bet that the science is sound and the market is enormous. That bet may be correct. Norovirus is responsible for approximately 21 million cases of vomiting and diarrhea annually in the United States, 109,000 hospitalizations, and 900 deaths — the majority among adults 65 and older, the same population at greatest risk of severe outcomes from flu. Globally, the disease causes an estimated 200,000 deaths per year, with the highest burden among children in low-income countries. In the United States alone, the economic cost of norovirus disease exceeds $5.5 billion annually in direct costs and lost productivity. No approved norovirus vaccine exists. The closest competitor to mRNA-1403, HilleVax's HIL-214 (spun out from Takeda), failed a Phase 2b trial in infants in July 2024 with a vaccine efficacy of just 5% — crashing the company's stock by roughly 80%. The failure did not end norovirus vaccine development — HilleVax is continuing adult studies — but it underscored how difficult the target is. Vaxart is also in development with an oral adenovirus-vector vaccine that targets gut-mucosal immunity rather than systemic antibody responses, with Phase 3 as a potential next step pending Phase 2 success and funding. That candidate takes a fundamentally different mechanistic approach but faces the same case-accrual problem. For adults, HilleVax's Phase 2b Navy trial demonstrated a vaccine effectiveness of 61.8% (95% CI, 20.8 to 81.6) for HIL-214 — a competitor candidate that showed proof-of-concept in controlled settings but has not advanced to a large-scale Phase 3 adult trial, as reviewed in published analyses of norovirus vaccine clinical development. Beyond Norovirus: Melanoma and Rare Disease on Track While the norovirus news dominated investor attention on Thursday, Moderna's oncology and rare disease programs remain on the pipeline's positive side of the ledger. Intismeran (mRNA-4157), the personalized cancer vaccine being developed with Merck, showed sustained benefit at five-year follow-up in a Phase 2b adjuvant melanoma study presented at the 2026 American Society of Clinical Oncology Annual Meeting in June, reducing the risk of recurrence or death by 49% compared to Merck's KEYTRUDA alone (HR=0.51; 95% CI, 0.294–0.887) and the risk of distant metastasis or death by 59%. Nine Phase 2 and Phase 3 trials across melanoma, non-small cell lung cancer, bladder cancer, and renal cell carcinoma are underway. Phase 3 adjuvant melanoma data are anticipated potentially before year-end 2026. Moderna's propionic acidemia therapeutic, mRNA-3927, has reached its target enrollment in its registrational study, with data also expected in 2026. On the commercial front, the company signed a manufacturing collaboration in Brazil for COVID vaccines, secured an EU joint procurement contract for up to 24 million doses of its RSV vaccine mRESVIA on behalf of six European countries, and received regulatory approvals in Australia and Mexico for mRESVIA and in Japan and Taiwan for mNEXSPIKE. What Tuesday's FDA Decision Could Change For a company burning through cash at a rate of roughly $2.3 billion annually, August 5 is not a routine milestone. Approval of mFLUSIVA would give Moderna a new commercial product arriving in time for the 2026–2027 flu season, new revenue that would reduce the per-quarter cash burn, and — perhaps most importantly — a regulatory signal that the mRNA platform can earn approvals against diseases that predate COVID. That signal matters to oncology investors who are watching whether the platform's credibility translates to diseases where the immunological challenges are far more complex. If the FDA does not approve mFLUSIVA — the most likely adverse scenario is a Complete Response Letter requesting additional data for adults 65 and older — Moderna has said it would continue to pursue approval with additional study. But the near-term commercial narrative would shift significantly. There is also a structural gap waiting even if approval comes: the CDC's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices — the body that normally translates FDA approval into clinical guidance about who should receive which vaccine and when — was disbanded by the current administration, as reported in TechTimes' June 2026 coverage. Without ACIP, clinicians will face uncertainty about whether mFLUSIVA is recommended preferentially, equivalently, or only in specific circumstances relative to existing high-dose flu vaccines for adults 65 and older. That uncertainty could delay uptake even after approval. The norovirus program, meanwhile, has no near-term commercial resolution. With an additional cohort still to enroll and case accrual dependent on unpredictable norovirus circulation, a definitive Phase 3 readout is now unlikely before the 2027–2028 timeframe at the earliest. But the underlying science — trivalent mRNA encoding norovirus capsid proteins, confirmed robust immune responses in Phase 1/2, no safety signal strong enough to stop the trial — has not changed. Moderna is hosting a live investor conference call on the morning of July 31, 2026, with an archived webcast to be available approximately two hours after it concludes on the Moderna investor relations website. Frequently Asked Questions What does it mean that Moderna's norovirus vaccine "failed the interim analysis"? It does not mean the vaccine was proven ineffective. A Phase 3 trial with a pre-specified interim analysis is designed to allow early stopping if the evidence is overwhelmingly positive. The statistical threshold for that early stop is intentionally set higher than the bar for the trial's final readout — because examining accumulating data multiple times inflates the risk of a false positive. Missing the early-success threshold means the current case count does not provide that overwhelming evidence. The trial remains blinded and ongoing. Moderna is enrolling additional participants to generate more cases, after which a standard final analysis will determine whether mRNA-1403 is protective. A missed interim bar is common in large vaccine trials and is not equivalent to a trial failure. When will a norovirus vaccine be available? No approved norovirus vaccine exists anywhere in the world. Moderna's mRNA-1403 remains the most advanced mRNA-platform candidate in Phase 3, but the trial now requires additional enrollment and case accrual across at least one more norovirus season before a final efficacy readout. A realistic timeline for regulatory submission, pending a positive result, would be no earlier than 2027–2028. HilleVax's adult program and Vaxart's oral vaccine candidate are also in development but at earlier stages. No competitor is positioned to reach approval before Moderna even under optimistic assumptions, as reviewed in coverage of the norovirus vaccine landscape. How does mRNA-1403 work, and is it different from the flu and COVID mRNA vaccines? mRNA-1403 uses the same lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery system as Moderna's COVID and flu vaccines. Where it differs is in the antigen: instead of encoding the influenza hemagglutinin protein or the COVID spike protein, it encodes the major capsid protein (VP1) of three norovirus genotypes — GII.4, GI.3, and GII.3 — each in a separate synthetic mRNA strand. Once injected, cells temporarily produce those capsid proteins, triggering the immune system to generate blocking antibodies and T cell responses targeted at the virus surface. Phase 1/2 data confirmed strong HBGA-blocking antibody responses against all three genotypes in both younger and older adults. What is Moderna's mFLUSIVA, and is it related to the norovirus vaccine? mFLUSIVA (mRNA-1010) is a separate product — Moderna's experimental mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccine, which shares the same LNP delivery platform as mRNA-1403 but encodes flu proteins rather than norovirus proteins. It has no direct clinical or scientific relationship to the norovirus trial. An FDA decision on mFLUSIVA is due August 5, 2026. An advisory panel voted unanimously in June to recommend it for adults 50 and older, making it the most likely near-term commercial positive for Moderna even as the norovirus program extends its timeline

With an additional cohort still to enroll and case accrual dependent on unpredictable norovirus circulation, a definitive Phase 3 readout is now unlikely before the 2027–2028 timeframe at the earliest. But the underlying science — trivalent mRNA encoding norovirus capsid proteins, confirmed robust immune responses in Phase 1/2, no safety signal strong enough to stop the trial — has not changed. Moderna is hosting a live investor conference call on the morning of July 31, 2026, with an archived webcast to be available approximately two hours after it concludes on the Moderna investor relations website. Frequently Asked Questions What does it mean that Moderna's norovirus vaccine "failed the interim analysis"? It does not mean the vaccine was proven ineffective. A Phase 3 trial with a pre-specified interim analysis is designed to allow early stopping if the evidence is overwhelmingly positive. The statistical threshold for that early stop is intentionally set higher than the bar for the trial's final readout — because examining accumulating data multiple times inflates the risk of a false positive. Missing the early-success threshold means the current case count does not provide that overwhelming evidence. The trial remains blinded and ongoing. Moderna is enrolling additional participants to generate more cases, after which a standard final analysis will determine whether mRNA-1403 is protective. A missed interim bar is common in large vaccine trials and is not equivalent to a trial failure. When will a norovirus vaccine be available? No approved norovirus vaccine exists anywhere in the world. Moderna's mRNA-1403 remains the most advanced mRNA-platform candidate in Phase 3, but the trial now requires additional enrollment and case accrual across at least one more norovirus season before a final efficacy readout. A realistic timeline for regulatory submission, pending a positive result, would be no earlier than 2027–2028. HilleVax's adult program and Vaxart's oral vaccine candidate are also in development but at earlier stages. No competitor is positioned to reach approval before Moderna even under optimistic assumptions, as reviewed in coverage of the norovirus vaccine landscape. How does mRNA-1403 work, and is it different from the flu and COVID mRNA vaccines? mRNA-1403 uses the same lipid nanoparticle (LNP) delivery system as Moderna's COVID and flu vaccines. Where it differs is in the antigen: instead of encoding the influenza hemagglutinin protein or the COVID spike protein, it encodes the major capsid protein (VP1) of three norovirus genotypes — GII.4, GI.3, and GII.3 — each in a separate synthetic mRNA strand. Once injected, cells temporarily produce those capsid proteins, triggering the immune system to generate blocking antibodies and T cell responses targeted at the virus surface. Phase 1/2 data confirmed strong HBGA-blocking antibody responses against all three genotypes in both younger and older adults. What is Moderna's mFLUSIVA, and is it related to the norovirus vaccine? mFLUSIVA (mRNA-1010) is a separate product — Moderna's experimental mRNA-based seasonal influenza vaccine, which shares the same LNP delivery platform as mRNA-1403 but encodes flu proteins rather than norovirus proteins. It has no direct clinical or scientific relationship to the norovirus trial. An FDA decision on mFLUSIVA is due August 5, 2026. An advisory panel voted unanimously in June to recommend it for adults 50 and older, making it the most likely near-term commercial positive for Moderna even as the norovirus program extends its timeline

news.content_title: Cryo-EM study reveals dynamic structure of human norovirus
news.content: Human norovirus is the leading cause of acute gastroenteritis worldwide and is estimated to infect 600–700 million people each year. Despite its enormous public health impact, no effective antiviral drugs are currently available. A detailed understanding of the three-dimensional structure of the virus is essential for elucidating its infection mechanism and developing effective therapeutics. However, research on human norovirus has been hampered by the inability to efficiently propagate the virus in cultured cells, making it difficult to obtain sufficient quantities of infectious particles for structural studies. In contrast, studies of murine norovirus, which can readily be propagated in cell culture, have shown that its capsid undergoes conformational changes in response to environmental conditions. Whether human norovirus exhibits similar structural dynamics has remained unknown. To address this question, the research team successfully produced virus-like particles (VLPs) of the human norovirus GII.3 strain, which has been responsible for repeated regional outbreaks, and determined their structures using state-of-the-art cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). Structural analysis revealed that a single VLP preparation contained two distinct conformational states, referred to as the resting and rising states, which differ in the location of the protruding (P) domain. Further analysis showed that (1) in the resting state, the P domain is positioned close to the underlying shell (S) domain and forms an extensive interaction network mediated primarily by the distal P2 subdomain. (2) In the rising state, the P domain is elevated by approximately 1 nm and rotated by about 55°, accompanied by a reorganization of the interaction network to the P1 subdomain. In addition, the P domain in the rising state exhibits substantially greater structural flexibility than in the resting state. These findings provide the first evidence that the human norovirus capsid, like that of murine norovirus, is not a rigid shell but a dynamic molecular assembly capable of adopting multiple conformations in response to its environment. Because the P domain contains both the host receptor-binding sites and the major antibody epitopes, these conformational changes may play important roles in regulating viral infectivity, receptor recognition, and immune evasion. Future studies will investigate the environmental factors-such as pH, metal ions, and physiological acids-that trigger these structural transitions, determine whether the same conformational changes as shown in murine norovirus occur in infectious virions, and explore the development of antibodies or small-molecule compounds capable of stabilizing or inhibiting these transitions. Such studies are expected to provide a foundation for the development of next-generation vaccines and novel antiviral therapies against human norovirus. Source: Journal reference: Song, C., et al. (2026). Conformational Plasticity of the Human Norovirus GII.3 Capsid Reveals Alternative P Domain Interaction Networks. International Journal of Molecular Sciences. DOI: 10.3390/ijms27156586. https://www.mdpi.com/1422-0067/27/15/6586
